title: No checksum/digest pinning on base image, Odin tarball, or raylib clone — posture is parity with the workflow, not beyond it
evidence:
FROM ubuntu:24.04
 && curl -fsSL "https://github.com/odin-lang/Odin/releases/download/${PIN}/${ASSET}" -o /tmp/odin.tar.gz \
 && tar -xzf /tmp/odin.tar.gz -C /opt/odin \
RAYLIB_TAG="6.0"
  git clone --depth 1 --branch "$RAYLIB_TAG" https://github.com/raysan5/raylib.git "$SRC"
detail: ubuntu:24.04 is a mutable tag; the Odin tarball and raylib tag-6.0 clone have no checksum/signature verification. This exactly matches the workflow's own curl -fsSL/no-checksum posture (parity bar), so no gap beyond CI — but the local fetch is cached in an image layer, so drift persists across runs.
recommended_fix: Optional hardening only: pin FROM ubuntu:24.04 by digest, verify a SHA-256 of the Odin tarball before tar -xzf, and note the parity decision in the Dockerfile comment.

title: .dockerignore excludes '_bmad' but not gitignored scratch under _bmad-output, so untracked/gitignored files still ship into the image
detail: The build context is the working tree, not a git checkout: the .dockerignore header's 'TRACKED tree' claim overstates. Gitignored review scratch (_charter-*.md) and 18MB of _bmad-output planning artifacts land in the image layer. Scan of this checkout found no secrets, so risk is low.
recommended_fix: Add '_bmad-output' (or at least '_bmad-output/**/review/') to .dockerignore, mirroring .gitignore, so gitignored scratch can never enter the image.

title: Container runs as the invoking uid: a uid-0 invoker runs the suite as root and can leave root-owned debris in the host bind mount
detail: --user $(id -u):$(id -g) is correct for non-root invokers (no root debris), and the design exposes no docker socket and only the goldens/_reports mount. But on Linux an invoker with uid 0 (common for devs) runs the container as root, writing root-owned files into the host-mounted reports dir.
recommended_fix: Warn or refuse when $(id -u) is 0 ('running as root — container will write root-owned files to goldens/_reports'), or document the requirement to invoke as a non-root user.
